title: The Gardener and the Squire
summary: Larsen was the master gardener of a noble Danish estate. With boundless love and science, he grew exquisite melons, rare artichokes, and magnificent flowers that won international...
full_text:
Larsen was the master gardener of a noble Danish estate. With boundless love and science, he grew exquisite melons, rare artichokes, and magnificent flowers that won international prizes and were served at the royal palace.

Yet the haughty squire and his lady constantly sneered at Larsen, claiming that foreign fruit from royal merchants was infinitely superior, until the King himself visited the castle specifically to honor Larsen and place a golden medal of merit upon the modest gardener's breast.

True excellence speaks for itself and outshines the envious blindness of pride.
moral: True genius in cultivation and art receives the acclaim of the world despite the snobbery of masters.
